claims.text: Somerset House is a massive neoclassical building complex situated on the Strand that directly overlooks the River Thames.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The current building sits on the site of a former Tudor palace that originally belonged to Edward Seymour, the 1st Duke of Somerset.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The present structure was designed by Sir William Chambers, with construction beginning in 1776 to create a grand space for government offices and learned societies.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Surprisingly, the building actually stood directly on the edge of the River Thames until the Victoria Embankment was constructed in the late 1860s.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The main courtyard features a beautiful bronze statue group by John Bacon that depicts the sea god Neptune alongside King George III.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Inside the building, the formal rooms of the learned societies were elaborately decorated with painted ceilings by renowned artists like Joshua Reynolds.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Since the early 21st century, the complex has been completely redeveloped into a vibrant cultural centre that hosts exhibitions and artist studios.
claims.subject: self
